title: Kubernetes Rolling Deployment Background Transaction Data Loss
businessContext: During automated CI/CD deployments of a payout processing worker service on Kubernetes, payouts occasionally get left in a half-processed `PENDING` state with missing bank transfers, requiring manual database surgery to reconcile balances.
problemStatement: When Kubernetes deploys a new replica set, it sends a `SIGTERM` signal to the old pods. The Node.js application immediately executed `process.exit(0)` inside the `SIGTERM` handler. Any background database transaction currently running mid-flight was aborted abruptly without rolling back or finishing, corrupting ledger balances.
constraints: Stop accepting new jobs from Redis / BullMQ / SQS queue.
Allow active in-flight transactions a graceful grace period (e.g. 15s) to complete.
Close database connection pools cleanly before exiting.
candidateTasks: Explain the Kubernetes pod termination lifecycle (`preStop`, `SIGTERM`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, `SIGKILL`).
Implement coordinated graceful shutdown: stop accepting new work -> wait for in-flight tasks -> close DB pools -> `process.exit(0)`.
Add a hard timeout fallback so the process exits even if a stuck connection hangs.
hints: On SIGTERM: 1) Stop listening to new HTTP requests / pause queue worker. 2) Wait for active operations. 3) Close database pool. 4) Set safety timeout (e.g. 15s) to force-exit if stuck.
Remember to call forceExitTimer.unref() so the safety timer does not keep the event loop alive on its own after all connections finish.

testCases.name: Coordinates graceful shutdown and finishes active jobs
testCases.explanation: Safely protects in-flight transactions during rolling restart.

alternativeApproaches: Using Kubernetes `preStop` hook with `sleep 5` before SIGTERM to allow load balancer iptables propagation.
commonMistakes: Not calling `forceExitTimer.unref()`, which can keep the event loop alive by itself.
Closing the database pool before waiting for active HTTP requests to complete, causing in-flight requests to fail with "Connection pool closed".
